# The Restaurant AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition


**by Mike Waldron**


## Why this report exists


For[restaurant](https://ottimate.com/industry/restaurants/) operators operating with tight margins, there’s not much room for error. So when prime costs climb past 65-70% of revenue, even small price discrepancies can take a toll on profitability. A broadliner invoice with a mispriced case of chicken, or a supplier slowly increasing prices across dozens of SKUs, can widen the gap between expected and actual food costs, leaving operators to guess whether waste, theft, or billing errors are to blame.


Most restaurant operators can sense when something’s amiss. But when food cost percentages look higher than expected, it can be difficult to determine whether it’s due to a recipe issue, a vendor billing error, or a coding mistake. This is especially true for lean AP teams that simply don’t have time for in-depth investigations. As a result, problems often go unresolved, and they continue to impact the bottom line.


Each quarter, Ottimate processes thousands of invoices for our restaurant customers. We’ve compiled that data into a snapshot to help restaurant operators quantify what’s really happening. It provides benchmarks based on actual restaurant AP data rather than industry estimates or survey responses.


The first edition of the Restaurant AP Automation Benchmark Report focuses on duplicate detection, fraud exposure, invoice discrepancies, payment errors, invoice lifecycle time, and AP labor savings. Twice a year, we’ll track how these numbers evolve and what’s driving the changes so restaurant operators can see how they stack up and where there are opportunities to improve performance.


## Duplicate detection


Restaurants remain the highest-volume duplicate detection segment across our entire customer base. That alone makes the
case: at this volume, manually catching duplicate invoices isn’t a realistic line of defense. Automated detection is doing
work no AP team could do by hand.


$773


average saved per duplicate invoice in 2025


$938


average saved per duplicate invoice in the first half of 2026


## Flagged before the check went out


More than half of accounts had an invoice flagged as risky in the first six months of 2026, up from 34.8% across all of 2025. A bad invoice rarely looks bad on its own. It looks wrong next to the last four, and that’s a comparison automated review makes on every invoice, every time, without anyone needing to remember what produce cost three weeks ago. As that comparison catches more, exposure that used to go unnoticed starts showing up before it becomes a loss.


34.8%


invoices flagged as risky in 2025


51%


invoices flagged as risky the first half of 2026


## The price that quietly stopped being the price


Six months into 2026, $256.7M in credits has already been uncovered, 61% of what all of 2025 turned up. Overcharges rarely look like overcharges: a case cost that moved eleven cents in March and never moved back or a promotional rate that quietly expired. What makes them findable is the memory of what that item cost last month and what the contract said it should cost, which is the part automation handles, and a kitchen manager approving invoices before the dinner rush reasonably cannot.


$420.7M


uncovered credits in all of 2025


$256.7M


uncovered credits in the first half of 2026


## The losses you can't claw back


Payment errors are costly and difficult to recover from once funds have left the account. Halfway through the year, this pace is already on track to approach last year’s full total by year-end. Manual payment reviews miss what a consistent, automated check catches every time, which is exactly why a final validation layer before disbursement matters.


14,250


payments with errors in all of 2025


6,026


payments with errors in the first half of 2026


## Invoice lifecycle time


Time saved per invoice climbed from 5.9 days to 8.8 days year over year, even as invoice volume per account rose 16 percent. Faster processing and rising volume are compounding each other. What that means in practice: the original labor-savings estimate now understates what’s actually being realized. As invoice counts grow, the time saved isn’t staying flat, it’s growing with it.


11 days


average invoice lifecycle time in 2025


2.2 days


average invoice lifecycle time in the first half of 2026

## About this report


The Restaurant AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition is published by Ottimate using aggregated, anonymized data from our restaurant customer base. All benchmarks reflect real invoice processing data across independent restaurants and multi-unit restaurant groups. This is the first edition; future editions will track trends and flag what’s driving the changes.
